## Findings
- claim-1: In `sources/0809.2981v2.tex` (revision `source-revision-9f2d90286b159738da58b0fe0bd47f85b5597dcdbd2b987cea65817b43536281`, SHA256 `9ddef409b3aa44eb1d31f101f3d22b364fdb5b52c404bc06529a2e3f6441bb02`), the quotient \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) has \(\mathbb Z\)-basis \(\{s_\lambda:\lambda\subseteq(n-r)^r\}\). Exact excerpt: “the \(\mathbb Z\)-submodule \(I_{r,n-r}\) spanned by all \(s_\lambda\) with \(\lambda\not\subseteq(n-r)^r\) forms an ideal” and “\(H^\star(G/P_J,\mathbb Z)\) has \(\mathbb Z\)-basis … \(=\{s_\lambda:\lambda\subseteq(n-r)^r\}\).” [source-2@L1318-L1330|claim=formal-document]
- claim-2: For the bigrassmannian corresponding to \(i^j\), the source states that \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) is generated as an ideal of \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) by the interval-indexed set \(\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(n-r)^r\}\). Exact excerpt: “\(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) is generated as an ideal of \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) by … \(=\{ s_{\mu}: i^j \subseteq \mu \subseteq (n-r)^r \}\).” [source-2@L1365-L1375|claim=formal-document]
- claim-3: The supplied formal-source excerpts do not state that the degree-\(d+k\) columns are the direct-sum interval component \(\bigoplus_{i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq q^r,\ |\mu|=d+k}\mathbb Zs_\mu\), nor that the *complete* \(h_1\)-row set is exactly \(\{h_1s_\lambda\}\) for all interval-indexed degree-\(d+k-1\) \(\lambda\). They also contain no bounded explicit Pieri-rule excerpt identifying those products as the requested rows.
## Strategy
Inspected `sources/0809.2981v2.tex`, revision `source-revision-9f2d90286b159738da58b0fe0bd47f85b5597dcdbd2b987cea65817b43536281`, SHA256 `9ddef409b3aa44eb1d31f101f3d22b364fdb5b52c404bc06529a2e3f6441bb02`.

- `source-2@L1318-L1330` states the ambient quotient basis: “\(I_{r,n-r}\) … forms an ideal” and “\(H^\star(G/P_J,\mathbb Z)\) has \(\mathbb Z\)-basis … \(\{s_\lambda:\lambda\subseteq(n-r)^r\}\).”
- `source-2@L1365-L1375` states ideal generation: “\(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) is generated as an ideal … by … \(\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(n-r)^r\}\).”

## Gaps
These bounded excerpts establish only the ambient Schur basis and an interval-indexed ideal generating set. They do not explicitly define the columns of the relevant free presentation as the interval-indexed Schur classes, nor state that its complete \(h_1\)-relation rows are precisely the products \(h_1s_\lambda\) over all corresponding interval-indexed \(\lambda\).

Thus the requested source certificate is **not established** from the inspected source excerpts.

## Next
A further source excerpt is required that explicitly specifies both the presentation’s column indexing and its complete \(h_1\)-Pieri row set.
